david.name: David
david.role: King named in many psalm headings
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: The collection remembers his worship, dangers, failures, and the promise concerning his royal line.
david.connections: Some headings connect songs with Saul, Absalom, and other people in David’s life.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: These associations place royal justice and household care within the collection.
solomon.connections: Psalm 72 concerns a just ruler. Psalm 127 concerns work, rest, and children.

asaph-singer.name: Asaph
asaph-singer.role: Name attached to a group of psalms
asaph-singer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asaph-singer.importance: The songs include judgment, questions about suffering, remembered history, and appeals after destruction.
asaph-singer.connections: The headings name Asaph in Psalm 50 and Psalms 73–83.

jeduthun.name: Jeduthun
jeduthun.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeduthun.importance: His name recalls the performance of prayers, not only their written words.
jeduthun.connections: The headings connect his name with musical directions for the songs.

sons-korah-psalms.name: The sons of Korah
sons-korah-psalms.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sons-korah-psalms.importance: The group’s songs preserve different experiences of worship rather than one steady mood.
sons-korah-psalms.connections: Their songs include longing for God, national defeat, Zion, and unanswered distress.

heman-ezrahite-psalms.name: Heman the Ezrahite
heman-ezrahite-psalms.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
heman-ezrahite-psalms.importance: The associated prayer continues without a closing answer or promise of immediate relief.
heman-ezrahite-psalms.connections: The heading also names the sons of Korah. The prayer describes isolation and approaching death.

ethan-ezrahite-psalms.name: Ethan the Ezrahite
ethan-ezrahite-psalms.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ethan-ezrahite-psalms.importance: The prayer holds remembered promise beside a difficult present experience.
ethan-ezrahite-psalms.connections: The song recalls a promise to David and asks about the king’s present humiliation.

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Leader remembered in songs and a heading
moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: His name connects rescue, prayer, and the cost of the people’s refusal to listen.
moses.connections: The collection recalls his work with Aaron and his prayers during the people’s failures.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
aaron.importance: The flowing oil on his beard gives Psalm 133 an image for shared blessing.
aaron.connections: The songs name his descendants, his prayers, and the people’s conduct toward him.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.role: One of those remembered for calling on God
samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
samuel.importance: His answered prayer belongs within the poem’s account of holiness, forgiveness, and correction.
samuel.connections: Psalm 99 names him with Moses and Aaron.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: His remembered promise gives the people a shared account of belonging.
abraham.connections: The songs connect his name with God’s people and the promise concerning the land.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.role: Ancestor named in the remembered promise
isaac.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
isaac.importance: His name connects successive generations within the account of a lasting promise.
isaac.connections: Psalm 105 recalls God’s oath to him between references to Abraham and Jacob.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.role: Ancestor remembered through both a life and a people
joseph.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joseph.importance: His name can recall the man or the people descended from him.
joseph.connections: Psalm 105 recalls his sale, imprisonment, and later authority in Egypt.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.role: Ancestor whose name also identifies Israel
jacob.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jacob.importance: Many songs use his name for the whole people rather than the living ancestor.
jacob.connections: Psalm 105 recalls his promised land and the family’s arrival in Egypt.

dathan.name: Dathan
dathan.role: Person remembered in the wilderness account
dathan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
dathan.importance: His fate appears among remembered failures that the people confess.
dathan.connections: Psalm 106 recalls the people’s failures and requests rescue.

abiram.name: Abiram
abiram.role: Person remembered in the wilderness account
abiram.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abiram.importance: The poem names his company while recalling rebellion in the wilderness.
abiram.connections: Psalm 106 recalls the people’s failures and requests rescue.

phinehas.name: Phinehas
phinehas.role: Person remembered in the wilderness account
phinehas.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
phinehas.importance: His intervention interrupts the plague in the poem’s remembered account.
phinehas.connections: Psalm 106 recalls the people’s failures and requests rescue.

melchizedek.name: Melchizedek
melchizedek.role: Priest named in an oath to the royal figure
melchizedek.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
melchizedek.importance: Later Christian and Church readers connect the royal and priestly images with Jesus Christ.
melchizedek.connections: Psalm 110 connects a priestly order with the ruler addressed in the song.

jesse.name: Jesse
jesse.role: David’s father named at the close of Psalm 72
jesse.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesse.importance: The family name identifies the remembered king as this section of the collection closes.
jesse.connections: The closing line refers to the prayers of David, son of Jesse.

sihon.name: Sihon
sihon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sihon.importance: His name connects praise with remembered conflicts before the people settled in the land.
sihon.connections: The songs recall his defeat while praising the gift of land.

og.name: Og
og.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
og.importance: His name connects praise with remembered conflicts before the people settled in the land.
og.connections: The songs recall his defeat while praising the gift of land.

sisera.name: Sisera
sisera.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
sisera.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sisera.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
sisera.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

jabin-judges.name: Jabin
jabin-judges.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
jabin-judges.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jabin-judges.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
jabin-judges.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

oreb.name: Oreb
oreb.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
oreb.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
oreb.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
oreb.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

zeeb.name: Zeeb
zeeb.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
zeeb.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zeeb.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
zeeb.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

zebah.name: Zebah
zebah.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
zebah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zebah.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
zebah.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

zalmunna.name: Zalmunna
zalmunna.role: Earlier enemy recalled in a prayer
zalmunna.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zalmunna.importance: The remembered name gives the plea an example of a threatening power already defeated.
zalmunna.connections: Psalm 83 asks for victory like the earlier defeats of Israel’s enemies.

saul.name: Saul
saul.role: King named in headings about David’s danger
saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul.importance: His pursuit supplies a remembered setting for several prayers about protection.
saul.connections: Headings name him in songs about rescue, reported hiding places, and threats.

absalom.name: Absalom
absalom.role: David’s son named in the flight heading
absalom.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
absalom.importance: The family conflict places the prayer for rest beside a threat from within David’s household.
absalom.connections: Psalm 3’s heading connects the prayer with David fleeing from him.

nathan-prophet.name: Nathan
nathan-prophet.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nathan-prophet.importance: The remembered confrontation supplies a setting for confession and a request for inward change.
nathan-prophet.connections: The heading connects his visit with David’s conduct toward Bathsheba.

bathsheba.name: Bathsheba
bathsheba.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bathsheba.importance: Her place in the heading keeps the confession connected with harm involving another person.
bathsheba.connections: The heading recalls David’s conduct toward her before Nathan’s visit.

doeg.name: Doeg
doeg.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
doeg.importance: The reported words provide context for a poem about destructive speech.
doeg.connections: The heading says he reported David’s visit to Ahimelech to Saul.

ahimelech-priest.name: Ahimelech
ahimelech-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahimelech-priest.importance: The report connects the poem’s warning about speech with a remembered visit.
ahimelech-priest.connections: Psalm 52’s heading names his house as the place David entered.

joab.name: Joab
joab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joab.importance: His name connects the song with a remembered conflict.
joab.connections: The heading recalls a battle against Edom in the Valley of Salt.

cush-benjamite-psalms.name: Cush the Benjamite
cush-benjamite-psalms.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
cush-benjamite-psalms.importance: The name supplies a setting for a plea that invites fair judgment of both sides.
cush-benjamite-psalms.connections: The heading connects David’s song with his words. It gives no further account of Cush.

abimelech-psalms.name: Abimelech in Psalm 34’s heading
abimelech-psalms.role: Ruler named in the heading about David
abimelech-psalms.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abimelech-psalms.importance: This heading introduces praise for rescue. It does not identify him with Genesis’s same-name rulers.
abimelech-psalms.connections: The heading recalls David acting insane and being sent away.

royal-king-psalm45.name: The king in the wedding song
royal-king-psalm45.role: Unnamed royal figure addressed in Psalm 45
royal-king-psalm45.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-king-psalm45.importance: The wedding’s honor stands beside a demand for fair rule.
royal-king-psalm45.connections: The song praises his strength and asks him to love justice and reject wrongdoing.

royal-bride-psalm45.name: The bride in the wedding song
royal-bride-psalm45.role: Woman addressed at the royal wedding
royal-bride-psalm45.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-bride-psalm45.importance: Her move into the royal household is celebrated through the language of a wedding.
royal-bride-psalm45.connections: The poem describes her approach, clothing, companions, and entry into the palace.

exiles-psalm137.name: The exiles beside Babylon’s rivers
exiles-psalm137.role: People forced from home who remember Zion
exiles-psalm137.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
exiles-psalm137.importance: Their grief turns into a violent wish for revenge, including harm to Babylon’s children.
exiles-psalm137.connections: Their captors ask for songs. The speakers refuse and remember Jerusalem’s destruction.
